rumours: Along Sentinel's Blue Quay, customs-inspectors and Forebear ship-captains are deadlocked over the new harbour-chain dues.
The Knights of the Candle have posted double watches around the royal necropolis after salt-witches were sighted near the sea-tombs.
In Kozanset's spice-souk, moneychangers say Daggerfall gold is trading at a discount until the Betony fishing truce is renewed.
Palace guards at Castle Sentinel have arrested two chart-thieves trying to copy the admiralty's soundings of the western shoals.
Silk-weavers in the upper bazaar complain that corsair blockades off Stros M'Kai have doubled the price of cyan dye-shells.
At the Order of the Scarab chapterhouse, scholars are examining an iron-bound chest dredged from a First Era Ra Gada war-galley.
Cistern-wardens beneath the palace terrace found fresh tunnel-work cutting toward the old treasury vaults.
Tavern-keepers by the camel-yards say a veiled Ansei pilgrim defeated three mercenary duellists with a unsharpened bronze rod.
legends: Castle Sentinel's great cyan dome was tiled with ten thousand glazed bricks baked in the kilns of Kozanset to mirror the Iliac sky.
When the First Warrior Wave landed at Sentinel Bay, the Forebear vanguard burned their own transports on the shingle so no man looked back to Yokuda.
The Order of the Candle was founded by royal widows who swore that no lamp in the Necropolis of Sentinel would ever go out before dawn.
During the War of Betony, Admiral Jahir chained twelve fireships together and steered them himself into the northern blockade.
Beneath Sentinel's Grand Bazaar lies the Great Cistern of Satakal, supported by eighty porphyry columns brought from the sunken islands.
King Camaron's judgement-seat on the palace porch is carved from a single block of white coral-limestone that sweats before a storm.
The bronze astrolabe atop the Admiralty Tower was calibrated by Yokudan star-pilots who navigated by the unmoving Warrior constellation.
Every New Life Festival, the Crown and Forebear elders of Sentinel exchange a cup of salt-water and a cup of oasis-water on the palace steps.
songs: Blue gleams the dome of Sentinel above the western sea, where galleys furl their striped sails along the limestone quay!
In Kozanset the spice-winds blow through alleys cool and narrow, and sword-smiths test the curved steel edge as keen as any arrow.
The Candle-Knights in cloaks of white pace round the royal dead, while harbour-lanternsrock and gleam in gold and crimson-red.
Look north across the Iliac where Daggerfall's grey towers stand—two crowns that watch the narrow strait between the sea and land!
Fill up the brass coffee-pot and lay the carpets down, to bargain for a bale of silk in Sentinel's high town.
When Forebear prows and Crown decrees agree upon the tide, no fleet upon the Abecean can match our navy's pride!
The cistern-water runs ice-cold beneath the bazaar floor, though noon-day sun beats white as bone outside the lattice door.
Long live the throne of Sentinel and Hunding's ancient way, that keeps the southern portal of the great Iliac Bay!

rumours: At Bergama's oasis gates, water-wardens measure every caravan's skin-ration twice since the southern qanat silted up.
Out in the Hollow Wastes, Ash'abah scouts have marked three ancestral tombs with white salt-ash to warn travellers of risen Ra Gada dead.
Prospectors returning from Volenfell swear the Dwemer brass-spiders walk the outer colonnades whenever the sand-wind exposes the bronze doors.
In Gilane's bazaar, spice-factors are paying high silver for scorpion-venom sacs and intact sand-serpent scales.
Nomad matrons at the Tigonus cisterns say the Kykos dust-witches are luring stray camels into the Web of Anker sinkholes.
At Tu'whacca's Throne, the silent priests have lit the blue necro-braziers—a sign that Withered Hand defilers are near.
Hegathe's cliff-wardens turned back a Forebear merchant train yesterday over an unpaid well-tithe from three seasons ago.
Caravan-bashis crossing the Salt Flats travel only by star-compass at night to avoid the noon heat-mirages and glass-scorpions.
legends: When Clan Rourken's chieftain threw Volendrung across Tamriel, the hammer fell in the heart of the Alik'r and named Volenfell.
The Lost City of the Na-Totambu preserves the Hall of Virtues where Frandar Hunding's sword-singers carved their final book of circles.
At Tu'whacca's Throne, the consecrated sand never shifts in any gale, holding the footprints of the first Ra Gada priests who blessed the necropolis.
The Ash'abah tribe accepted the curse of ritual exile so that someone among the Redguards could cut down dishonoured ancestors when necromancers wake them.
Hegathe withstood the First Warrior Wave on sheer sea-cliffs until the Forebear captains swore the Compact of the Wells.
Beneath the great dune-sea of the Alik'r run seven stone-lined qanats dug by Yokudan water-diviners who listened to the earth with bronze bowls.
At Leki's Blade, the goddess of aberrant swordsmanship clove a sandstone mountain in two with an ephemeral spirit-sword to end a fratricidal war.
Whoever breaks the Well-Oath at an Alik'r oasis is given a full waterskin punctured with a needle and pointed toward the deep erg.
songs: March by the stars across the erg when silver shines the dune, and rest beneath the date-palm shadefrom tierce until the noon!
Keep clean the blade and pure the tomb, as Tu'whacca decrees,and never draw water from the well before you bend your knees.
At Volenfell the brass gates sleep beneath the drifting sand, where Rourken's hammer struck the rock and claimed the desert land.
The Ash'abah rides out alone with ash upon his brow, to lay the restless grandfathers who broke their burial vow.
From Hegathe's white cliff-bastion to Bergama's cool spring, the caravan-bells chime in time like anklets on a string!
Beware the sink of Anker's Web where yellow scorpions creep, and wind-carved pillars hide the pits where ancient serpents sleep.
At Leki's school upon the ridge the wooden practice-sword teaches the wrist to turn the stroke before a word is roared.
Though kingdoms rise and empires fall beyond the mountain wall, the Alik'r sand remembers only honour after all!

rumours: At Hallin's Stand, town-reeves are repairing the southern watch-towers after desert raiders tested the canyon road at dusk.
Garrison engineers at the Bangkorai Pass have requisitioned forty waggon-loads of cut stone to reinforce the lower portcullis.
Miners at Onsi's Breath say the deep copper-veins echo with Dwarven piston-beats from the sealed galleries of Klathzgar.
In the oasis gardens below the pass, date-growers have hired bowmen to drive off the cliff-harpies fouling the irrigation channels.
A messenger from Evermor arrived at the border gate with word that Reachfolk war-bands are probing the northern canyon rim.
Priests at the Fallen Wastes cenotaphs report grave-robbers searching for the five symbolic swords of Ansei Hallin.
Caravan-factors waiting at the pass-hostelry are paying twenty septims a day for reliable escorts down into the Alik'r.
Alchemists near Nilata Ruins warn that the waterfall mists have turned bitter since necromancers occupied the upper Ayleid vaults.
legends: Bangkorai Garrison has never been taken from the south since its cyclopean wall was wedged between the twin canyon cliffs in the First Era.
When Emperor Hestra's legions marched on Hallin's Stand, Ansei Symmachus Hallin and five companions hid the Five Swords and fought until the desert swallowed the host.
At Onsi's Breath, the warrior-god Onsi is said to have exhaled upon the red rock, turning brittle shale into veins of pure malleable copper.
The Nilata waterfall plunges out of an Ayleid sky-well built by exiles who fled Cyrodiil before the Alessian orders could burn their star-charts.
Klathzgar's bronze foundry-doors were cast with an acoustic lock that opens only when struck in the rhythm of a Rourken forge-hammer.
The bridge at Ephesus was arched by Breton and Redguard masons who met at the keystone and cemented it with wine from both valleys.
On the crags above the Garrison stand the Seven Watch-Stones, each naming a century in which the pass held High Rock and Hammerfell apart.
They say when Hammerfell faces its darkest hour, the bronze war-horns buried beneath Hallin's obelisk will sound without mortal breath.
songs: Between the green of Bjoulsae's vale and Alik'r's burning sand, the great stone wall of Bangkorai divides the western land!
At Hallin's Stand the obelisk still keeps the Ansei's name, who met the legion shield to shield and put an empire's pride to shame.
Dig deep in Onsi's copper-pit where red the canyon glows, and smelt the bronze for hilt and boss while mountain water flows!
The Garrison portcullis hangs on chains as thick as thighs—no army marches through the pass beneath the wardens' eyes.
From Nilata's white waterfall down to the desert floor, the caravan-mules pick their way along the canyon shore.
Five swords were hidden in the stone when Hallin's circle fell, and five true hearts shall draw them forth when rings the alarm-bell!
Here Breton slate gives way to domes of sandstone warm and red, and cedar-shaded courtyards rise where palm-tree fronds are spread.
Keep sharp the watch on Bangkorai, where North and South are met, and never let the border-gate its ancient charge forget!

rumours: In Belkarth's caravanserai, Dragonstar factors are hiring veteran delvers to clear the iron-mines along the northern escarpment.
Star-gazers near the impact craters say the green sky-glass hums louder whenever the constellations align above the tableland.
At the Elinhir cross-roads, Colovian wine-carters and Redguard drovers are pooling guards against the Scaled Court raiding parties.
Arena bookmakers in Dragonstar are offering three-to-one odds against anyone surviving five rounds with the new crag-minotaurs.
Sappers working the Balamath delve broke into a Yokudan star-vault sealed with celestial wards and living stone gargoyles.
Miners at Rahni'Za report that ancient sword-disciples still pace the terraced training-courts when the canyon fog rises.
Water-sellers in Belkarth have raised the price of sweet cistern-water after mineral runoff tainted the lower crater pools.
A Nord caravan-captain from Falkreath is recruiting axemen at the tavern to reopen the snow-choked pass behind Dragonstar.
legends: Elinhir's apex towers were raised by Nedic star-priests who aligned every street and lintel with the autumn rising of the Warrior and the Thief.
At Rahni'Za, the School of the Blades trained generations of Ansei initiates who carved their practice-circles into the living red granite.
When the sky-shards fell across Craglorn, the desert sand fused into green volcanic glass around every crater rim.
Dragonstar was divided down its central market-brook when Nordic highlanders and Crown governors signed the Treaty of the Split Shield.
Beneath the Star-Gazers' Observatory lies a subterranean astrolabe of bronze and quartz that tracks the constellations even at noon.
The Buried Tombs of the Na-Totambu in Craglorn were hidden inside box-canyons so steep that coffins had to be lowered by bronze cranes.
At Skyreach Pinnacle, the Nedic kings built their last sun-bastion high above the clouds before the Ra Gada sword-singers climbed the stair.
They say a blade quenched in the mineral water of a Craglorn star-crater will never rust or lose its edge against scaled hide.
songs: High on the red mesa-top where stars burn close and cold, the towers of old Elinhir guard secrets unretold!
In Belkarth's yard the camels kneel beside the mountain wain, where Colovian and Redguard meet upon the table-plain.
Climb up the stair to Rahni'Za with wooden sword in hand, and learn the five-and-thirty cuts that won the western land!
At Dragonstar the market-brook divides the town in twain—Nordic timber on the north and sandstone on the plain.
Where green glass rims the starfall pit upon the canyon floor, the scorpion and the crystal-wraith keep watch forevermore.
Wager your gold at Dragonstar when arena-trumpets blow, and watch the gladiator's steel flash in thetorchlight's glow!
From Falkreath's pines to Bangkorai the high road winds in stone, across the windy tableland where eagles hunt alone.
Look to the Warrior in the sky and keep your compass true—the crags of Craglorn test the heart of every traveller through!

rumours: At Taneth's red-cliff harbour, Crown magistrates have impounded three coaster-barks suspected of running contraband arms to the passes.
In Rihad's border-bazaar, Forebear factors and Colovian horse-traders are hiring outriders to clear the goblin-tribes from Scarp Keep.
Pass-wardens at Dragon's Mouth Caverns say an Orc war-band from the iron mesas has occupied the old toll-bastion.
Copper-smelters in the Dragontail gorges report harpy matriarchs nesting in the ruined aqueduct arches above the road.
At Lainlyn's bluff-citadel, falconers are training cliff-hawks to intercept carrier-pigeons sent by rival bay syndicates.
Quarrymen cutting red sandstone above Skaven uncovered a sealed Ra Gada catacomb whose bronze lamps were still burning.
Mule-drivers on the Skaven turnpike carry iron-shod staves and sulfur-torches to ward off canyon sabre-cats at dusk.
A sword-smith in Taneth is offering a bag of gold for meteoric iron recovered from the high Dragontail scree-slopes.
legends: The Dragontail Mountains took their name from the serrated red-rock spine that coils from the Iliac Bay to the Colovian border.
Taneth's cliff-citadel was carved into arose-red sandstone promontory where seven terraced gardens are fed by mountain snow-melt.
At Rihad on the Brena River, Forebear and Imperial captains built the Bridge of Oaths with a toll-gate at each end and a shrine in the middle.
Skaven's round war-keep was raised at the crossroads of the four great wadis so its signal-mirrors could flash word to both coasts in an hour.
In Dragon's Mouth Caverns, a hot sulfur wind blows out of the mountain's throat every dusk, sounding like a sleeping wyrm's breath.
The Orc smiths of the Dragontail mesas learned to alloy red mountain copper with black iron during the long truces with the Crown emirs.
Lainlyn's cliff-stair has three hundred and sixty-five cut steps, one for each day the founders held the promontory against the sea-reavers.
They say the pass-cairns on the Dragontail crest must be given a white quartz pebble by every traveller, or the canyon mists will hide the trail.
songs: Red rise the fangs of Dragontail above the canyon road, where copper-mules with jingling bells bear down their heavy load!
In Taneth by the southern sea the terraced gardens bloom, while high above the harbour-boom stands fast the citadel-dome.
Cross Brena's bridge at Rihad town where Crown and Empire meet, and hear the anvils ringing out along the armourers' street!
At Skaven in the windy pass the signal-mirrors flash, and outriders in crimson cloaks across the wadis dash.
Beware the Dragon's Mouth at dusk when sulfur-vapours rise, and goblins watch the narrow gorge with yellow lantern-eyes!
From Lainlyn's bluff the falcons stoop above the bay so blue, and bring the word of returning ships before the watch-horn's blew.
Throw one white stone upon the cairn before you top the crest, that Tava's wind may guide your mule and grant your journey rest.
Whether by coast or canyon-track you ride through Hammerfell, the red crags of the Dragontail will test your saddle well!

rumours: In Abah's Landing, the Merchant Lords have hired extra Iron Wheel bailiffs to patrol the cantilevered bridges above the souk.
Dock-divers in the sunken cisterns claim the Thrallmaster's slavers have been using the flooded Yokudan vaults as a hidden careenage.
At No Shira Citadel, privateer captains are refitting their xebecs after sightings of a giant sea-serpent off the southern cape.
Moneychangers in the lantern-courts whisper that a single unstamped ledger stolen from the customs-house could topple two syndicates.
Spice-factors along the spice-quays pay quiet protection-dues in the Thriving Provisioner rather than risk their bales sinking at anchor.
Tomb-wardens near Prince Hew's Shuttered Tomb say the limestone sinkholes flood at high tide, trapping anyone still inside the vaults.
Fishermen on the karst headlands report eerie blue phosphor glowing around the shipwrecks on the Shark's Teeth reefs.
An apothecary in the lower rookeries is buying dreugh-wax and pearl-dust brought up from the sea-caves.
legends: Peninsula Hew's Bane was named when theYokudan engineering prince Hew cut a storm-Breakwater through the limestone cape and flooded half his own road.
Abah's Landing grew across seven tidal islands linked by arched stone bridges and timber sky-walks where no royal tax-collector ever set foot.
Prince Hew's Shuttered Tomb was built with bronze water-clocks that seal the inner burial chamber whenever the Abecean tide rises above the sill.
No Shira Citadel has changed hands nineteen times between merchant-princes, admirals, and corsair-kings without its lighthouse ever going dark.
The Sunken Cisterns beneath Abah's Landing are large enough to float a thirty-oar galley beneath the pavement of the Grand Souk.
When an Imperial fleet tried to blockade the harbour chain, the harbour-divers sawed through their rudders by lantern-light under water.
In the Thriving Provisioner's back room hangs a rusted iron key said to unlock the original charter-chest of the Free Syndicates.
Every captain who clears Abah's Landing throws a handful of roasted coffee-beans onto the breakwater to pay Tava for a fair land-breeze.
songs: Walk light upon the bridge-spans high in Abah's Landing town, where merchant-lords in silk kaftans look from their loggias down!
Keep one hand on your scimitar and one upon your purse, for in the alleys of the Bane a blink can cost you worse.
The Iron Wheel may march the quay with halberd and with badge, yet shadows slip across the roofs from parapet to ledge!
When high tide fills the Shuttered Tomb and drowns the marble stair, Prince Hew himself counts up the gold of those who lingered there.
Off Shark's Teeth Reef the breakers foam above the sunken prows, where coral grows on bronze cannon and barnacles on bows.
At No Shira the beacon-fire shines red across the strait, to warn the spice-xebecs away from rocks that lie in wait.
Down in the cistern-vaults below the bazaar's noisy floor, the smugglers row with muffled oars behind a secret door!
Here's to the free peninsula where syndics rule the bay—if you have coin in Abah's port, no question stops your way!

rumours: At Port Hunding's careenage, Restless League privateers are loading grapnels and pitch-pots for a cruise along the gold-lanes.
Delvers near Bthzark say the Dwemer steam-conduits under the island have been venting scalding brass-smoke since the last tremor.
In Saintsport, fishermen have hauled up bronze gears and cut-glass lenses in their nets half a league off the southern headland.
Headman Bhosek's bailiffs at the palace gate are charging five septims wharfage on every foreign keel that drops anchor in the cove.
At the Pillar of the Singing Sun, islanders leave offerings of fresh dates and honey before sailing out into the Abecean.
Shipwrights by the rope-walk claim a sunken Imperial treasure-hulk shifted on the outer coral shelf during last week's squall.
Tavern-bards at the Screaming Mermaid know six different versions of Prince A'tor's last stand in the bay.
The observatory-wardens on the western cliff have locked the brass telescope-dome afterrogue arcanists tried to pry out the sky-lenses.
legends: Port Hunding marks the exact beach where Frandar Hunding's fleet first beached their prows and built the Pillar of the Singing Sun.
Bthzark's subterranean machine-halls were constructed by Rourken Dwemer who harnessed the island's volcanic sea-vents to turn giant brass Orreries.
During the Battle of Hunding Bay, Cyrus the Restless lured Admiral Richton's flagship onto the coral shoals and freed the island.
The Dwemer Observatory on Stros M'Kai was aligned to track both the stars above and the deep ocean currents of the Abecean Sea.
At the Grave of the Stranded, the ribs of three ancient sea-leviathans stand bleached in the sand where the first settlers built their huts.
Prince A'tor's soul-gem blade was said to glow like a forge-coal whenever a loyal Crown warrior stood within a cable's length.
Saintsport's freshwater spring bubbles up cold and sweet through porous coral-rock less than twenty paces from the salt surf.
No captain of the Restless League will weigh anchor on a Friday unless a gull alights upon the main-yard before sunrise.
songs: Drop anchor in Port Hunding's cove where palm-trees fringe the sand, and Frandar Hunding's sun-pillar looks out across the land!
Beneath the hills of Stros M'Kai the brass of Bthzark turns, where deep within theDwemer vaults the steam-fire ever burns.
Remember Cyrus on the deck when Richton's galleons came—he cut the hawser with his sword and set the bay aflame!
At Saintsport by the coral reef the pearl-divers go down, and bring up shells of mother-of-pearl for Sentinel's high crown.
In the Screaming Mermaid's lantern-light the corsairs clink their gold, and sing of fifty boarding-fights in days of Restless old!
The brass dome on the western cliff looks out upon the night, and tracks the wandering planets' course in wheels of crystal light.
Heave short the cable, sheet the lateen sail against the breeze—from Stros M'Kai the xebecs fly across the southern seas!
Though small our island in the main, her name is known afar, where every wave in Hunding Bay reflects the Warrior's star!
